title: Participation within the scope of CONFIDENCE – Primary care-based, stepped, cross-sectoral care concept for people with post-acute infection syndromes – CONFIDENCE-part
summary:
Background
After an infection (such as Coronavirus or Epstein-Barr virus), long-lasting symptoms can occur that severely limit the daily lives of those affected. The CONFIDENCE project is developing a new care concept to improve the treatment of these patients. A key part of the project is the active involvement of patients and medical professionals. They share their experiences to help design things like questionnaires or treatment procedures.

Objective
This accompanying study examines how well the collaboration between the various participants (patients, professionals, and the project team) works. The goal is to find out how the involvement of these groups influences the development of the project and how the roles and tasks of those involved are perceived.

Methods
Participants in this study include members of patient advisory boards, professionals (such as doctors or therapists), and members of the project team. The study includes:

Surveys: Participants complete an online questionnaire at three different times during the project. In these surveys, they describe how they perceive the collaboration and their involvement. In addition, general information (such as age or profession) is requested once.

Analysis of Minutes: Reports and minutes from meetings that are already taking place will be scientifically evaluated afterwards. All names and personal details will be removed so that no individual person can be identified.
conditions: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS), defined as persistent symptoms chronologically related to a COVID-19 infection (Post-COVID syndrome) or other infections (e.g., Epstein-Barr virus or respiratory infections). This includes post-infectious Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and autonomic dysfunctions (e.g., postural tachycardia syndrome). Additionally, the participation of patients and stakeholders in health services research is examined.

interventions.name: Within the CONFIDENCE project, a participatory approach is pursued for the development of the intervention and evaluation components as well as for the project implementation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Membership in one of the following groups within the CONFIDENCE project:

- Members of the patient advisory board or representatives of patient organizations.

- Members of the stakeholder advisory board or representatives of stakeholder organizations.

- Members of the CONFIDENCE project team.

2) Provision of written or electronic informed consent for participation in the accompanying study.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Lack of informed consent for study participation.

2) Persons who are no longer actively involved in the advisory boards or the CONFIDENCE project team at the time of the survey.
